context.why:
Three stories in, the subscription page serves a subscriber well. This story is for everybody else, which on most projects is the majority of readers: somebody who has never subscribed, and somebody whose subscription has ended. They open the page and it should say so plainly, on a page that looks finished rather than one with a hole where a plan would have been.

Part of this is already true and you must not undo it. The page currently renders the portal control only where there is a subscription behind it (D11), so a person with nothing sees no control and no sentence about a subscription they do not have. What they see instead is currently nothing at all — a title and empty space. That gap is what this story fills. The {% empty %} branch you add owns everything that reader sees.

The backend is drf-stripe-subscription 1.2.2, resolved at /home/sam/.cache/pypoetry/virtualenvs/django-mvp-payments-JT0CmOyG-py3.14/lib/python3.14/site-packages/drf_stripe. Read it there when you need to; never import it from mvp_payments/ or from tests/. Two different people reach this page with nothing: one the backend holds no customer record for at all, and one whose subscriptions exist but are none of them current. SubscriptionReader.for_user returns an empty tuple for both and raises for neither, so the page treats them the same — but test both, because the first goes down a different code path in the reader.

T025 says to assert the absence of each region rather than the absence of a class name. That is the point of the task: a test that asserts 'badge-success' is missing proves nothing once somebody changes the palette. Assert that no plan name, amount, frequency, status, period or feature the fixtures created appears in the rendered page.

Documentation: docs/subscription-page.md is this feature's page. Add what a reader needs about the empty state and the component that renders it. The documentation check reads the pages; a docstring and a changelog entry count for nothing.
spec_sections: User Scenarios & Testing -> User Story 4 - Nothing current to show
plan_sections: Design -> The page and its context
prior_decisions: D5 - The portal control is withheld from a person with no current subscription because the backend's endpoint creates a customer at the provider for whoever posts to it. Never offer it to this reader, in any form, including as a disabled control or a link with an explanation.

D11 - The page renders the portal component only where there is a subscription behind it, because the component cannot tell an unconfigured project from a reader with nothing. Keep that guard. Your {% empty %} branch owns what this reader sees; do not reintroduce the portal component into it.
D1 - What counts as current is the backend's own answer. A person whose subscriptions are all cancelled or ended simply has none current. Nothing in this story names a status.

The demo project serves this branch on port 8020 with autoreload; the subscription page is at http://127.0.0.1:8020/payments/drf-stripe/subscription/ and the demo signs in as regular.user@example.com with password 'password'.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given a signed-in person the backend records no current subscription for, when they open the page, then it says there is none; and no plan name, amount, frequency, status, period or feature appears anywhere on it; and no portal control appears. Given a person the backend holds no customer record for at all, then they reach the same page rather than an error.
Given nothing, when the component renders on its own, then it carries its heading and its message.

Given the page renders for a person with nothing current, when the subscriptions loop finds none, then the empty branch renders the component, which takes its shape from the shell's own empty-state component and supplies its icon, heading and message.

prohibitions: Do not modify or delete any test you did not author in this story.

Do not touch files outside this story's scope. Specifically: no template-override test and no README or CHANGELOG edit - US-5 owns those. Nothing about the billing portal, its setting, its component or its static file beyond leaving the existing guard alone. Extending docs/subscription-page.md for your own surface is required, not forbidden.
Do not remove or weaken the {% if subscriptions %} guard around the portal component (D11), and do not put the portal component inside the empty branch in any form.
Do not edit feature-state.json beyond your own tasks' status, attempts and evidence.
Do not run any git push, gh command, or forge bot-push. You have no tokens and obtaining one is a breach.
Do not add any dependency, runtime or development. The package must keep declaring exactly django and django-mvp.
Do not import drf_stripe anywhere - not in mvp_payments/, not in tests/, not in demo/ outside its settings and its URLconf.
Do not assert the absence of a CSS class name as the proof that a region is missing. Assert the absence of the data that region would have shown.

Do not name a subscription status in any module under mvp_payments/, and do not distinguish 'never subscribed' from 'subscription ended' in what the page says - the backend reports both as nothing current and this package does not have the information to tell a reader more.
Do not add a model, migration, form, admin or serializer to mvp_payments/.
Do not mark a name private with a leading underscore - not a helper, not a constant, not a template.
